thesis: The pipeline IS the hero. Instead of a stock screenshot or an abstract gradient, the fold shows a real, live-looking terminal running an actual Cadence pipeline file — stage by stage, with a status column that updates. The rest of the page is the same idea zoomed out: each feature band is one stage of 'how a deploy actually gets safer', paced like a pipeline itself (define → watch → gate → ship).

macrostructure.name: Workbench
macrostructure.reason: brief's centre of gravity is a tool the reader will run, not a story to read — the page should look and feel like the product before a word is read

primary.application: the hero's control surface is a framed terminal (traffic-light dots + tab title, all aria-hidden, non-focusable) running `cadence run deploy.yaml`; stage rows populate with a status glyph (queued → running → passed) via CSS/JS state classes, degrades to fully-passed static state with no JS and under reduced-motion

supporting.application: one large, heavily-blurred amber bloom behind the hero terminal on a near-black base, low opacity, kept clear of the fold's headline text so worst-pixel contrast is never at risk; absent in lower sections to keep it a single fold-level moment, not a page-wide wash

signature_devices.count_check: 2 devices total (1 primary + 1 supporting) — within the 'one or two' ceiling

palette.base: near-black surfaces, three elevation steps (base #0a0b0d / raised #121317 / overlay #1a1c21)
palette.foreground: off-white #eef0f2 primary text, muted #9aa0aa secondary text
palette.accent_primary: amber/copper (~45° hue) — the 'cadence/metronome pulse' signal color, used for the primary CTA, running-stage glyphs, and the light-leak bloom
palette.accent_secondary: desaturated teal (~185° hue) — used only for 'passed' status glyphs, i.e. a semantic success color distinct from the brand accent
palette.why_not_violet: explicitly avoided the indigo/violet/magenta AI-glow band (taste-rubric ai-cliche-gradient territory); amber was chosen for its tempo/pulse connotation and because it reads as a terminal/signal color, not a SaaS-default one

families.display_and_body: system sans stack (-apple-system, 'Segoe UI', 'Inter', system-ui, sans-serif) — no remote font fetch permitted under the file:// / offline constraint, so the scale and weight contrast carry the expressiveness instead of a custom face
families.mono: system mono stack (ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', 'Cascadia Code', 'Roboto Mono', monospace) for the terminal, code snippets, and stage labels — reinforces the dev-tool register

typography.notes: tight negative tracking on display sizes, roman only (no italic headings), body 1.6 leading / display 1.05-1.15, uppercase reserved for short mono labels only

spacing.target: high (airy/gallery) — base unit 8px, section gaps scale up substantially between Workbench hero and feature bands to let each stage of the narrative breathe

specifics: hero terminal: staged reveal of pipeline rows (queued->running->passed), a blinking block cursor on the prompt line, all via CSS animation + prefers-reduced-motion:reduce fallback to the fully-passed static frame
section entrances: small opacity/translateY reveal on scroll, staggered per item, ease-out, ~200-300ms
hover: buttons and cards get a short transform/opacity feedback, ease-out ~180ms, no overshoot
focus rings appear instantly, never transitioned

depth.target: mid, tipping rich only in the hero — a 3-step elevation ramp (base/raised/overlay), soft background-tinted shadows, the terminal window is the one 'raised' object competing with the light-leak for attention

iconography.policy_resolution: asset policy calls for the official Phosphor package; this is a single static offline file with no build/package step, so Phosphor's npm package cannot be vendored in. Resolution: hand-authored inline SVG line icons, ONE family, ONE stroke weight (1.75px), sized on a 16/20/24 ramp, functioning as a deliberate offline substitution for Phosphor — recorded here per generation-craft-defaults.md's exception rule ('name the rule, reason, and evidence reference')

section_architecture.layout_model: fixed hairline-bottom bar, wordmark left, 3 links + CTA right
section_architecture.composition_anchor: amber underline tick under the active/hover link, echoing the metronome-pulse motif in miniature
section_architecture.content_dependency: minimal — this is a tool, not a marketing site with deep IA
section_architecture.responsive_transform: links collapse to a single 'Docs' link + CTA under 640px; wordmark stays

section_architecture.purpose: state what Cadence is and prove it in the same glance
section_architecture.layout_model: Workbench split — headline/lede/CTA column left, live terminal window right, light-leak bloom behind the terminal
section_architecture.composition_anchor: the terminal window itself — first thing the eye lands on because it is the only object with real elevation + motion on load
section_architecture.content_dependency: the terminal runs a real, readable deploy.yaml-shaped pipeline (build -> test -> gate:approval -> deploy) so the product is legible without prose
section_architecture.responsive_transform: stacks to single column under 768px, terminal moves below the copy and drops to a shorter 4-row view so it still fits without scroll-jacking

section_architecture.purpose: name the problem in one honest sentence before pitching the fix
section_architecture.layout_model: Long-Document single column, generous measure, no card
section_architecture.composition_anchor: one short paragraph set larger than body copy, acting as a pull-quote without needing a fabricated quote
section_architecture.content_dependency: directly names the 'chat pings and tribal knowledge' pain from the audience state in the brief
section_architecture.responsive_transform: measure narrows proportionally, no structural change needed at this simplicity

section_architecture.purpose: stage 1 of the narrative — pipelines are defined as code
section_architecture.layout_model: Feature Stack band #1 — code panel left, copy right
section_architecture.composition_anchor: a syntax-colored YAML snippet (not a screenshot) as the proof object
section_architecture.content_dependency: the YAML shown here is the same pipeline shape referenced in the hero terminal, so the two sections visually rhyme
section_architecture.responsive_transform: code panel stacks above copy under 768px, font-size steps down one notch, horizontal scroll container for long lines instead of wrap

section_architecture.purpose: stage 2 — live status while it runs
section_architecture.layout_model: Feature Stack band #2, mirrored — copy left, status-list mock right
section_architecture.composition_anchor: a compact vertical stage list with glyphs (reuses the icon set, teal for passed) instead of a repeated code panel — deliberate layout variation, not a recolor of band #1
section_architecture.content_dependency: shows the same 4 stages from the hero/code example progressing, tying the three sections into one thread
section_architecture.responsive_transform: band mirrors to copy-first order on narrow widths (reading order beats visual mirroring) and the status list becomes full width

section_architecture.purpose: stage 3 — the risky step waits for a human
section_architecture.layout_model: Feature Stack band #3 — centered single card, full width either side, distinct from the two-column bands above
section_architecture.composition_anchor: a single 'awaiting approval' card with a shield glyph and two disabled-look decorative action buttons (not real controls, marked appropriately) — the odd-one-out composition signals 'this step is different in kind', not just content
section_architecture.content_dependency: directly answers 'what stops an unreviewed deploy' — the feature the audience is most skeptical will exist
section_architecture.responsive_transform: card width caps and centers at all sizes; padding compresses on narrow viewports rather than the card losing its centered composition

section_architecture.purpose: the actual CTA moment — respects a developer audience by giving them a command, not a form
section_architecture.layout_model: Stat-led-adjacent but honest: one large mono command line is the composition anchor, no fabricated number attached to it
section_architecture.composition_anchor: an oversized copyable command in a raised panel with a copy-to-clipboard control
section_architecture.content_dependency: the command matches the CLI implied by the hero terminal ('cadence run …' family)
section_architecture.responsive_transform: command panel scales font down and allows horizontal scroll rather than wrapping a shell command, at all widths

section_architecture.purpose: close the page, minimal legal/nav residue
section_architecture.layout_model: single hairline-top row, wordmark + 3 links + one line, no four-column link farm (deliberately not the 'AI footer' default)
section_architecture.composition_anchor: restraint itself is the composition choice here
section_architecture.responsive_transform: row wraps to two lines under 480px, no structural change

layout_model_count_check: distinct layout models used: fixed-bar nav, Workbench split, Long-Document paragraph, Feature-Stack two-col (x2, mirrored), single centered card, command panel, footer row — well over the 'two layout models minimum for 3+ sections' floor
consistency_axis: not applicable — first generation in this output directory, no established design system/token registry to inherit from
